description: Validate one OKLCH palette per Space across browser chrome, address fields, panels, and native Settings, including contrast and restart.
preconditions: Replay, compile, and package the exact recorded bundle; launch only the isolated Dev profile
Use acceptance-owned Spaces and record their names and colors
steps: Create two Spaces; open Settings from the first and choose a saturated color with the existing Space colors picker
Inspect chrome, Command-L address field and results, Command-T panel, MRU, Peek, and Settings; change controls and panels saturation
Enable decorative effects, keep the main glow fixed, and drag each secondary glow independently; on release verify the native window uses that point's saved color and new position
Change Panels saturation and Light/Dark mode; verify derived UI roles change while authored glow colors, placement, size, and intensity remain intact
Switch to the second Space, choose a different color, and confirm both Spaces retain their own palettes
Open Settings from each Space; retarget while a picker interaction is pending and confirm no edit reaches the other Space
Check Auto, Light, and Dark; inspect black and white pages with bright and dark seeds, minimum opacity, visible glows, and grain
Check Solid and native glass materials; verify text, icons, focus, and selected results remain readable
Disable decorative background customization; edit a Space color and verify palette updates without glows or grain, then re-enable effects and verify the saved recipe returns
Quit normally, relaunch the same profile, verify both recipes and dials, then close and quit
observables: The existing Settings picker and Space creation/editor write the same Space recipe; no independent Controls accent or panel Tint color picker remains
Palette changes propagate live to the initiating Space's windows and panels
Chroma dials preserve chosen colors and lightness while changing derived saturation
The palette derives from the authored glow colors; the renderer never replaces those colors with generated tones or scales them with Panels saturation
Each glow keeps its own position, size, and intensity; moving a secondary point updates its native glow without moving the main point
Paired field and panel surfaces keep text and selection readable over black and white content, including minimum material opacity
Color edits preserve material enablement; disabled decoration keeps its saved recipe while the palette and contrast floor still apply
Edits and delayed callbacks never change another Space or a deleted Space
Normal restart preserves colors, harmony, mode, and chroma dials; closing surfaces and quitting causes no new crash
